To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the integration between usual care provider and SME programs is not always high, but it can be high, medium or low; (ii) in most cases, the usual care provider is the primary care physician; (iii) patient behaviors and/or outcomes are positive in most of the cases; (iv) the integration level is not a predictor of the outcomes, but the results are more positive when the integration level is high.
Diabetes SME produces positive effects on health outcomes, independently from the degree of integration with usual care.

(i) the integration between usual care providers and diabetes self-management education programs is not always clear, and (ii) when patients/participants perceive that the usual care provider is more involved in the delivery of the diabetes self-management education program, the results are more positive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of diabetes SME programs in usual care.
the level of integration of SME programs within usual care, and the possible differences across them.
the integration between diabetes self-management education and usual care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more the usual care provider is involved in the diabetes SME program the more positive the outcomes.
the level of integration of usual care and diabetes SME is not a determinant factor for the effectiveness of SME.
there is a need for more research to identify which level of integration between the two systems is more effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, regardless of the integration level, SME programs are effective in improving health status and health behaviors.
the level of integration of the diabetes SME programs with the usual care is not related to the outcomes of the programs, but it could affect the patients' perception of the programs.
, regardless of the level of integration, the SME program is a valuable resource to improve diabetes care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of SME programs into the usual care is an essential factor to ensure the success of the programs.
the integration level of SME programs within the usual care is an important factor to consider when planning and delivering diabetes education.
the level of integration of diabetes SME into the usual care is variable and that this variability does not affect the outcomes of the programs.
